pages.canonicalText:
START
H OW TO U S E T H I S O N YO U R P H O N E
No zoom. No glossary
wall. One mental model
at a time.
1 · Read “IN ONE BREATH”
If you cannot explain the definition in one breath, reread it.
2 · Read the ridiculous memory hook
Silly is deliberate. Weird images are easier for your brain
to retrieve under interview pressure.
3 · Predict the real example
Before reading the explanation, ask what the code/system
will do and why.
4 · Say the interview answer aloud
Do not memorize it word-for-word. Keep the structure:
definition → purpose → example → trade-off.
5 · Name one failure mode
That final trade-off is what often makes an answer sound
mid-level instead of junior.

pages.canonicalText:
The mid-level answer
engine
1. WHAT?
Give a clean definition with the correct noun. “A CDN is a
geographically distributed delivery/cache layer...”
2. WHY?
Name the engineering pressure it solves: latency,
correctness, maintainability, concurrency, cost, security...
3. EXAMPLE?
Make it concrete in ordinary product code. Browser → API
→ cache → database beats abstract vocabulary.
4. TRADE-OFF?
Say what it costs or when you would not use it. Mid-level
engineers know tools create new problems too.
5. FAILURE MODE?
Show that you can operate software, not just design happy
paths: stale cache, race, retry storm, leaked secret, slow
query...

MAP
T H E L E A R N I N G R OA D M A P
Start with the web. End
with AI systems.
Study in order once. After that, jump by section based
on interview weakness.
01 WEB, NETWORKING & DELIVERY
How browser requests travel, get routed, cached, and returned.

Who you are, what you may do, and how systems defend the
path.

How persistent data stays related, correct, and fast under
concurrency.
04 REALTIME & ASYNC JAVASCRIPT
How apps wait, stream, schedule, and react without freezing.
05 JAVASCRIPT CORE MENTAL MODELS
The language behaviors behind most interview gotchas.
06 TYPESCRIPT & REACT FOUNDATIONS
Types, components, state, effects, identity, and reuse.
07 FRONTEND PLATFORM, UX & PERFORMANCE
Rendering, accessibility, loading, navigation, and perceived
speed.

plans, migrations, and scale.

nonsense or collapsing when dependencies slow down.

001
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
HTTP
I N O N E B R E AT H
The request-response protocol used by browsers,
apps, and servers to exchange web data. It is the basic
language behind APIs, pages, images, and most web
traffic.
M A K E I T S T I C K
HTTP is a waiter: you order GET /pizza; the kitchen
sends a response.
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /users/42 -> 200 + JSON user data.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
HTTP is a stateless request-response protocol. I use
methods, headers, status codes, and bodies to define
the contract between client and server.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 001 / 310

002
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
HTTPS
I N O N E B R E AT H
HTTP carried through TLS so traffic is encrypted and
the server can prove its identity. It protects credentials,
tokens, and user data from easy interception or
tampering.
M A K E I T S T I C K
HTTP is shouting your password across a cafe.
HTTPS is whispering through a locked tube.
R E A L E X A M P L E
https://example.com/login encrypts the request
while it travels over the network.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
HTTPS is HTTP over TLS. TLS gives confidentiality,
integrity, and server authentication.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 002 / 310

TLS
I N O N E B R E AT H
A security protocol that establishes an encrypted,
integrity-protected connection between peers. It is
what makes HTTPS trustworthy in transit.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Two spies agree on a secret code, then talk where
everyone can hear but nobody can understand.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Browser verifies a certificate, negotiates keys,
then sends encrypted HTTP.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
TLS provides encryption, integrity, and authentication
for network connections; HTTPS uses TLS underneath.

DNS maps names to records such as IP addresses so
clients can locate services.

IP address
I N O N E B R E AT H
A network address used to identify where packets
should be delivered. Networking needs an addressable
destination for hosts and interfaces.

need the port to find the right door.

uses a larger address space.

An IP address identifies a network endpoint.
Applications usually reach it indirectly through DNS.

006
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Port
I N O N E B R E AT H
A numeric identifier that distinguishes services on the
same host. One machine can run a web app, database,
cache, and more at the same IP.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Same apartment building, different doorbells: 3000
for the app, 5432 for Postgres.
R E A L E X A M P L E
localhost:5173 and localhost:8000 reach
different processes on the same computer.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A port selects the service or process at a host address;
the combination of protocol, host, and port helps identify
an endpoint.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

009
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
HTTP methods
I N O N E B R E AT H
Standard verbs that express what operation a request
intends to perform. They make API contracts
predictable and communicate semantics to clients,
caches, and infrastructure.
M A K E I T S T I C K
GET looks, POST creates, PATCH edits, DELETE
throws it in the bin.
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /users reads; POST /users creates; PATCH /
users/42 updates part; DELETE removes.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use HTTP methods according to their semantics: GET
for retrieval, POST for creation/actions, PUT for
replacement, PATCH for partial updates, DELETE for
removal.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

010
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
HTTP status codes
I N O N E B R E AT H
Three-digit codes that summarize the outcome of an
HTTP response. They let clients handle success,
redirects, client errors, and server errors consistently.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A restaurant scorecard: 2xx "here is dinner", 4xx
"you ordered nonsense", 5xx "the kitchen is on fire".
R E A L E X A M P L E
200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad
Request, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, 500, 503.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I treat 2xx as success, 4xx as client-side request/auth
issues, and 5xx as server-side failures; specific codes
matter for client behavior.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

Query parameters
I N O N E B R E AT H
Key-value values appended to a URL after ? to alter
how a resource is retrieved. They are convenient for
filtering, sorting, searching, and pagination.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You order "pizza?size=large&spicy=true" instead of
inventing a new pizza endpoint.
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /products?
category=laptops&page=2&sort=price.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use query parameters for optional modifiers such as
filters, sort order, search terms, and pagination.

Path parameter
I N O N E B R E AT H
A dynamic segment in a URL path used to identify a
specific resource or nested location. It gives stable,
readable resource addresses.
M A K E I T S T I C K
/dogs/fluffy means "the dog named Fluffy", not "all
dogs with ?dog=fluffy".
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /users/42 where 42 is the user ID.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Path parameters usually identify a concrete resource,
while query parameters usually modify how a collection
is retrieved.

REST models resources and uses HTTP semantics
consistently. I focus more on clear resource contracts
than on blindly following naming rules.

API
I N O N E B R E AT H
A defined interface through which software
components communicate. It separates
implementation details from the contract consumers
rely on.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A vending machine exposes buttons and a coin slot;
you do not need to know its internal gears.

Frontend calls /api/orders; a payment service
exposes a create-payment API.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
An API is a contract between software components.
Web APIs often use HTTP, but APIs can also be libraries,
OS interfaces, or messaging contracts.

back into data.

Serialization turns runtime data into a portable
representation such as JSON; deserialization
reconstructs usable data from it.

servers behind it.

022
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Reverse proxy
I N O N E B R E AT H
A proxy that sits in front of backend servers and
receives client traffic on their behalf. It hides internal
topology and can terminate TLS, route, cache, rate-
limit, and load balance.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The hotel front desk chooses which staff member
handles your request; guests never call room 412
directly.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Nginx receives api.example.com and forwards /
auth to one service and /orders to another.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A reverse proxy is the public entry point in front of
servers. I use it for routing, TLS termination, load
balancing, caching, and security controls.

what happens on misses.

I N O N E B R E AT H
A lookup where the requested value is absent or

Time To Live: how long a cached or leased value
remains valid before expiring. It bounds staleness and
prevents data from living forever.

A carton says "good for 60 seconds"; after that,

freshness; long TTLs improve hit rate but increase
staleness risk.

Cache invalidation
I N O N E B R E AT H
Removing or updating cached data when the
underlying truth changes. Without invalidation, fast
responses can be confidently wrong.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You changed your haircut but the family group chat
still uses your 2012 profile photo.
R E A L E X A M P L E
After PATCH /users/42, delete or update cache
key user:42.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Cache invalidation is the consistency problem of
keeping cache aligned with the source of truth. I choose
TTL, explicit invalidation, or versioned keys based on
requirements.

A server that can handle each request without relying
on request-specific state stored only in its own local
memory. Any replica can serve the next request, which
simplifies horizontal scaling and failover.

Any cashier can serve you because your loyalty card
carries what they need; cashier #3 does not
"remember" you personally.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Auth info comes from a token or shared session
store instead of process memory.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Stateless application servers keep request state outside
a specific instance, making load balancing and
horizontal scaling easier. SECTION

Stateful system

A system whose behavior depends on state
remembered across interactions. Many real systems
need durable or connection-specific state; the
challenge is managing it safely.

maintains live connections.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Stateful systems retain information across operations.
They are not bad; they simply require deliberate
persistence, replication, and failure handling.

segments.text: Stateful system

segments.sectionTitle: I N O N E B R E AT H
segments.text: I N O N E B R E AT H

segments.sectionTitle: I N O N E B R E AT H
segments.text: A system whose behavior depends on state remembered across interactions. Many real systems need durable or connection-specific state; the challenge is managing it safely.

segments.sectionTitle: M A K E I T S T I C K
segments.text: M A K E I T S T I C K

segments.sectionTitle: M A K E I T S T I C K
segments.text: The bartender remembers your open tab. If you switch bars, the new bartender has no clue.

segments.sectionTitle: R E A L E X A M P L E
segments.text: R E A L E X A M P L E

segments.sectionTitle: R E A L E X A M P L E
segments.text: A database persists orders; a WebSocket server maintains live connections.

segments.text: S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W

segments.sectionTitle: S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
segments.text: Stateful systems retain information across operations. They are not bad; they simply require deliberate persistence, replication, and failure handling.

or tokens.

036
S E C U R I T Y, I D E N T I T Y & T R U S T
Session
I N O N E B R E AT H
Server-recognized state that ties a sequence of
requests to an authenticated user or interaction. HTTP
is stateless, so sessions provide continuity.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The cloakroom gives you ticket 123; the desk uses it
to find your coat later.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Cookie contains session ID abc; server maps abc
-> user 42 in a session store.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A session associates requests with server-side state,
commonly through a secure session identifier stored in a
cookie.

S E C U R I T Y, I D E N T I T Y & T R U S T
Cookie
I N O N E B R E AT H
Small browser-managed data associated with a
domain and sent according to cookie rules. Cookies
are the standard mechanism for sessions, preferences,
and some tracking.

A website sticks a tiny labeled Post-it in your
browser and asks for it again later.

Set-Cookie: session=abc; HttpOnly; Secure;
SameSite=Lax.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Cookies are browser-managed key-value data with
security and scope attributes; they are commonly used
for session identifiers.

038
S E C U R I T Y, I D E N T I T Y & T R U S T
HttpOnly cookie
I N O N E B R E AT H
A cookie marked so browser JavaScript cannot read
it. It reduces exposure of session secrets to JavaScript
during many XSS scenarios.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The cookie is in a locked lunchbox: the browser can
deliver it, but your JS cannot open it.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Set-Cookie: session=abc; HttpOnly; Secure.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
HttpOnly prevents client-side JavaScript from reading a
cookie, which is useful for session credentials, though it
does not eliminate XSS impact.

039
S E C U R I T Y, I D E N T I T Y & T R U S T
JWT
I N O N E B R E AT H
A compact signed token format containing claims,
represented as header.payload.signature. It lets a
recipient verify that claims were issued by a trusted
signer without a database lookup for every verification.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A concert wristband says "VIP" and has an
unforgeable stamp; anyone can read VIP, but they
cannot fake the stamp.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Authorization: Bearer <jwt> containing sub, exp,
and roles.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
JWTs are signed claim containers, not automatically
encrypted. I validate signature, issuer, audience, and
expiry rather than trusting decoded payloads.

041
S E C U R I T Y, I D E N T I T Y & T R U S T
Refresh token
I N O N E B R E AT H
A longer-lived credential used to obtain new access
tokens without asking the user to sign in again. It
balances user convenience with short-lived access
credentials.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Your train season pass lets you print today's ticket;
you do not wave the season pass at every ticket
gate.
R E A L E X A M P L E
When access token expires, client sends refresh
token to auth server for a new access token.

contextual escaping, safe DOM APIs/framework

sanitization.

SQL injection

A vulnerability where attacker-controlled input
changes the structure or meaning of a SQL query. It
can expose or modify entire databases.

You ask a robot to find "Bob" and the user secretly

parameterized `WHERE email = $1`.

I prevent SQL injection with parameterized queries/
prepared statements and never concatenate untrusted
input into SQL syntax.

pages.canonicalText:
048
DATA B AS E S & DATA I N T E G R I T Y
Database
I N O N E B R E AT H
A system for persistently storing, querying, and
updating application data. Applications need durable
state that survives process restarts.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Your app's memory is a goldfish; the database is the
notebook it writes everything into.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Orders, users, and payments live in PostgreSQL
instead of a Node process variable.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A database provides durable storage plus query/update
mechanisms and consistency guarantees appropriate to

valid referenced row, unless nullability or cascading
rules say otherwise.

Database index

A data structure maintained to make particular
lookups or orderings faster. Without useful indexes,

reads. I design them around actual query patterns and
verify with query plans.

SQL JOIN
I N O N E B R E AT H
An operation that combines rows from related tables
based on a condition. Normalized relational data is
intentionally split across tables and must often be
recombined when queried.

You match a pile of name tags with a pile of lunch
orders using the same student ID.

SELECT u.name,o.total FROM users u JOIN orders o
ON u.id=o.user_id.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
JOINs combine related rows. I know INNER JOIN for
matching rows and LEFT JOIN when I need all left-side
rows even without matches.

054
DATA B AS E S & DATA I N T E G R I T Y
Transaction
I N O N E B R E AT H
A group of database operations treated as a single
logical unit that commits or rolls back. It prevents
partial updates that would leave business data
inconsistent.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Moving a cake: either the whole cake reaches the
table or we pretend the move never happened; half a
cake is not a valid transaction.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Debit account A and credit account B inside
BEGIN...COMMIT; on failure ROLLBACK.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Transactions make related writes atomic and provide
isolation guarantees so partial business operations are
not persisted.

ACID
I N O N E B R E AT H
A mnemonic for transaction properties: Atomicity,
Consistency, Isolation, Durability. It summarizes the
guarantees expected from robust transactional
databases.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A = all-or-nothing; C = rules stay sane; I = shoppers
do not trample each other; D = the receipt survives a
power cut.
R E A L E X A M P L E
A committed order survives restart; concurrent
updates respect the chosen isolation level.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
ACID describes transactional guarantees. I pay
particular attention to isolation level and business
invariants rather than treating the acronym as magic.

Optimistic locking
I N O N E B R E AT H
A concurrency strategy that allows reads freely but
rejects an update if the record changed since it was
read. It avoids heavy locks when conflicts are
uncommon.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You edit a shared document version 7; if someone
already saved version 8, your version 7 save is
rejected.
R E A L E X A M P L E
UPDATE docs SET ..., version=8 WHERE id=1 AND
version=7; zero rows means conflict.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Optimistic locking detects conflicts using a version/
timestamp and asks the caller to retry or resolve when
concurrent changes occur.

Offset pagination
I N O N E B R E AT H
Pagination that skips a numeric number of rows,
commonly with LIMIT and OFFSET. It is simple and
supports jumping to page numbers.

Tell the librarian: skip the first 40 books, give me the

SELECT ... ORDER BY id LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40.

Offset pagination is easy but large offsets can be slow
and inserts/deletes can shift results between requests.

DATA B AS E S & DATA I N T E G R I T Y
Cursor pagination
I N O N E B R E AT H
Pagination that continues after a stable sort key or
opaque cursor rather than a row count. It handles
large, changing feeds more efficiently and consistently.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Bookmark the last book you read instead of counting
4,820 books from the entrance every time.
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /feed?after=opaqueCursor; query uses WHERE
created_at < lastSeen ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 20.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Cursor/keyset pagination uses the last sort position,
avoiding large offsets and reducing duplicate/missing
items in changing datasets. SECTION

R E A LT I M E & AS Y N C JAVAS C R I P T
Asynchronous operation
I N O N E B R E AT H
Work that can complete later while the program
remains able to do other work. I/O often spends time
waiting, so async models improve responsiveness and
concurrency.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Order coffee, get a buzzer, sit down, and do
something else until it vibrates.
R E A L E X A M P L E
fetch() returns a Promise; await pauses the
async function without blocking the whole
runtime thread.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Asynchronous code represents completion in the future,
commonly through promises/callbacks. await improves
readability but does not make the underlying I/O
synchronous.

R E A LT I M E & AS Y N C JAVAS C R I P T
JavaScript event loop
I N O N E B R E AT H
The runtime mechanism that coordinates the call
stack with queued asynchronous callbacks/jobs. It
explains ordering, responsiveness, and why long
synchronous tasks freeze JavaScript UIs.
M A K E I T S T I C K
One chef cooks one active dish at a time; assistants
handle timers and deliveries, then put finished
tickets back in the chef's queue.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Promise callbacks enter the microtask queue;
timers run from a task queue after the stack is
clear.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
JavaScript runs synchronous code on a call stack. The
event loop schedules queued work when the stack is
free, with microtasks processed at defined checkpoints.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

R E A LT I M E & AS Y N C JAVAS C R I P T
Call stack
I N O N E B R E AT H
The stack data structure the runtime uses to track
active function calls. It determines where execution
returns and why deep recursion can overflow.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A stack of cafeteria trays: the last tray placed on top
is the first one removed.
R E A L E X A M P L E
a() calls b(), b() calls c(); frames unwind c ->
b -> a.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
The call stack holds execution frames for active
functions. Long synchronous work monopolizes it;
unbounded recursion can overflow it.

R E A LT I M E & AS Y N C JAVAS C R I P T
Microtask queue
I N O N E B R E AT H
The high-priority job queue used for Promise
reactions and related microtasks. It affects exact
async ordering and can starve later tasks if abused.
M A K E I T S T I C K
VIP queue: promise callbacks enter before the next
normal timer gets its turn.
R E A L E X A M P L E
console.log("A");
Promise.resolve().then(()=>console.log("B"));
console.log("C") => A,C,B.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Promise callbacks run as microtasks. After the current
stack finishes, the runtime drains microtasks before
moving to the next task such as a timer.

J AVAS C R I P T C O R E M E N TA L M O D E L S
async / await
I N O N E B R E AT H
Syntax for writing Promise-based asynchronous code
in a sequential-looking style. It makes async control
flow and error handling easier to read.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You write "wait for pizza" in the recipe, but the whole
restaurant does not freeze while your pizza bakes.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const r = await fetch(url); const data = await
r.json();
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
async/await is syntax over Promises. await suspends the
async function until settlement; it does not block the
JavaScript runtime from processing other work.

072
J AVAS C R I P T C O R E M E N TA L M O D E L S
try / catch
I N O N E B R E AT H
Language syntax for handling exceptions thrown
during execution, including rejected promises when
awaited. It lets code recover, translate, log, or surface
errors deliberately.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Put a trampoline under the risky acrobat so a fall
becomes a handled event instead of chaos.
R E A L E X A M P L E
try { await save(); } catch (err)
{ showError(err); }
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
try/catch handles exceptions. With async/await it
catches rejected awaited Promises, and I avoid
swallowing errors without context.

Closure
I N O N E B R E AT H
A function plus access to the lexical variables from
the scope where it was created. Closures power
encapsulation, callbacks, hooks, and private state
patterns.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A function leaves home but keeps a backpack
containing the variables from home.
R E A L E X A M P L E
createCounter() returns a function that keeps
access to count after createCounter returns.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A closure lets a function retain access to its lexical
environment after the outer function has finished.

074
J AVAS C R I P T C O R E M E N TA L M O D E L S
Scope
I N O N E B R E AT H
The rules that determine where a variable name is
visible and accessible. Correct scope prevents
accidental coupling and name collisions.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Your toothbrush belongs in your bathroom, not
magically in every room of the city.
R E A L E X A M P L E
A const declared inside a block is inaccessible
outside that block.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
JavaScript has lexical scope. let/const are block-
scoped; var is function-scoped, which is one reason I
prefer let/const.

075
J AVAS C R I P T C O R E M E N TA L M O D E L S
var, let, const
I N O N E B R E AT H
JavaScript declaration forms with different scoping
and reassignment behavior. Choosing predictable
declarations reduces bugs and communicates intent.
M A K E I T S T I C K
const is "do not replace this box"; let is "this label
may point somewhere else"; var is the weird uncle
from older JavaScript.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const user = {...}; let page = 1; avoid var in
modern application code.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I default to const, use let when reassignment is required,
and avoid var because of function scope and hoisting
behavior.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

076
J AVAS C R I P T C O R E M E N TA L M O D E L S
Hoisting
I N O N E B R E AT H
JavaScript's declaration processing behavior that
makes some bindings/functions known before the line
where they are declared. It explains surprising access
rules and the temporal dead zone.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The theater has your name on the seating chart
before you sit down, but security may still stop you
entering early.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Function declarations can be called before their
textual declaration; let/const cannot be
accessed before initialization.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Declarations are processed before execution, but
behavior differs: function declarations are callable early,
while let/const are in the temporal dead zone until
initialized.

you would choose a different tool.

077
J AVAS C R I P T C O R E M E N TA L M O D E L S
Primitive values
I N O N E B R E AT H
JavaScript values that are not objects: string, number,
boolean, undefined, null, bigint, and symbol. Their
copy/equality behavior differs from objects.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A primitive is like a printed number on a card;
copying the card gives you another value, not a
shared mutable box.
R E A L E X A M P L E
let a=5; let b=a; b=9 does not change a.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Primitives are immutable value types. Assigning them
copies the value, unlike object references that can point
to shared mutable objects.

J AVAS C R I P T C O R E M E N TA L M O D E L S
Reference semantics
I N O N E B R E AT H
Objects are accessed through references, so multiple
variables can refer to the same underlying object. It
explains mutation bugs and React identity behavior.

Treating existing data as unchanged and creating new
values for updates. It makes state transitions easier to

Immutability means producing a new value rather than
mutating existing state. It is especially useful in UI state
management and concurrent code.

Spread operator
I N O N E B R E AT H
The ... syntax used to expand iterable values or copy
enumerable object properties into a new structure. It

S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Spread is convenient for shallow copies and
composition, but nested objects remain shared unless I
copy the nested level too.

Array.reduce
I N O N E B R E AT H
An array method that accumulates many elements
into a single result. It can compute totals, groups,
maps, and other aggregates.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Everyone empties coins into one jar; the jar is the
accumulator.

S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
reduce folds a collection into one accumulator. I use it
when that improves clarity, but I do not force every loop
into reduce.

Spread/Object.assign make shallow copies. Nested
objects remain shared, so immutable nested updates
must copy each changed level.

Deep copy

A copy that recursively duplicates nested data instead
of sharing the same nested object references. It can
isolate structures, but full cloning can be costly or
semantically wrong for special objects.

document and every subfolder too.

supported structured-clone values.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A deep copy duplicates nested structures. I use
structuredClone when appropriate, but usually prefer
targeted immutable updates over cloning an entire
graph. SECTION

T Y P E S C R I P T & R E AC T F O U N DAT I O N S
TypeScript
I N O N E B R E AT H
JavaScript plus a static type system checked before
runtime. It catches many integration mistakes earlier
and documents contracts for humans and tools.
M A K E I T S T I C K
JavaScript lets you put soup in a USB port;
TypeScript yells before you try.
R E A L E X A M P L E
function add(a:number,b:number):number { return
a+b; }
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
TypeScript adds static checking and developer tooling
but erases to JavaScript at runtime; it cannot replace
runtime validation of untrusted data.

Interface
I N O N E B R E AT H
A TypeScript declaration describing the expected
shape/capabilities of an object or class. It makes
contracts explicit and reusable.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A job description says "must have id and name"
without caring who the employee is.
R E A L E X A M P L E
interface User { id:number; name:string }
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
An interface describes a structural contract. TypeScript
is structurally typed, so compatible shapes can satisfy
the interface.

093
T Y P E S C R I P T & R E AC T F O U N DAT I O N S
Union type
I N O N E B R E AT H
A type that allows a value to be one of several
alternatives. It models finite UI states and domain
choices safely.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The traffic light can be "red" | "amber" | "green" and
not "banana".
R E A L E X A M P L E
type Status = "loading" | "success" | "error".
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Union types model alternatives. Combined with

useEffect
I N O N E B R E AT H
A React hook for synchronizing a component with
systems outside React after rendering. It is the correct
boundary for subscriptions, imperative APIs, timers, and
similar external synchronization.
M A K E I T S T I C K
React finishes arranging the room, then useEffect
tells the outside world to turn on the music.
R E A L E X A M P L E
useEffect(()=>{ window.addEventListener(...);
return ()=>remove... },[]).
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use effects to synchronize with external systems, not
as a default place for derived state or event logic that
can happen directly.

T Y P E S C R I P T & R E AC T F O U N DAT I O N S
Effect cleanup
I N O N E B R E AT H
The function returned from an effect to undo the
previous subscription/resource before rerun or
unmount. It prevents duplicate listeners, stale
subscriptions, and leaks.
M A K E I T S T I C K
If you rent a karaoke machine, cleanup is returning it
instead of quietly collecting 40 karaoke machines.
R E A L E X A M P L E
return () => clearInterval(id) or unsubscribe().
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Effect cleanup reverses the previous effect. React runs it
before the effect re-synchronizes and when the
component unmounts.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

you would choose a different tool.

incorrect synchronization.

Derived state
I N O N E B R E AT H
A value computed from existing props/state instead of
stored independently. Avoiding duplicate state
prevents synchronization bugs.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Do not store first name, last name, AND full name in
three notebooks when full name is simple addition.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const fullName = `${firstName} ${lastName}`.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
If a value can be calculated cheaply from current props/
state, I derive it during render rather than storing and
syncing another state variable.

value. I choose controlled vs uncontrolled based on
validation, coordination, and performance needs.

requirements justify the complexity.

useCallback

A React hook that caches a function reference until

S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
useCallback memoizes function identity. I use it
selectively when referential stability prevents real work,
not as default boilerplate.

Prop drilling
I N O N E B R E AT H
Passing data through intermediate components solely
so deeper descendants can receive it. Too much
drilling creates noisy coupling, though a few levels can
be perfectly fine.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Passing a sandwich through five people who do not
want lunch just to reach person six.
R E A L E X A M P L E
App -> Layout -> Page -> Panel -> Avatar all
receive user only for Avatar.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Prop drilling is not automatically bad. I tolerate simple
explicit passing and introduce context/composition/store
only when the dependency is genuinely cross-cutting.

Lazy loading
I N O N E B R E AT H
Deferring loading or initialization until a resource is
actually needed. It reduces initial work and improves
startup performance.

scene starts.

Settings")); images use loading="lazy".

Lazy loading moves non-critical work off the initial path.
I balance smaller startup cost against later loading states
and network waterfalls.

expensive feature boundaries.

application code/assets for development or
production. Browsers and deployments need
optimized, loadable output from a large source tree.

A moving company finds every box referenced by
your packing list, labels them, compresses them, and
loads the truck.

Vite/Rollup resolves imports, transforms
modules, splits chunks, hashes assets.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A bundler follows the module graph and produces
optimized assets; modern tools also handle dev serving,
HMR, code splitting, and asset processing.

Hydration
I N O N E B R E AT H
Attaching client-side React behavior to HTML that was
rendered on the server. SSR HTML must become
interactive without throwing it away and rebuilding
blindly.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A mannequin already looks dressed; hydration gives
it a nervous system so the buttons actually work.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Server sends <button>Buy</button>; React
hydrates and attaches event behavior using
matching markup.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Hydration connects client React to existing server-
rendered markup. Server/client output must be
compatible to avoid mismatches.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

you would choose a different tool.

HTML. ARIA changes accessibility semantics; it does not
automatically add keyboard behavior.

API loading states
I N O N E B R E AT H
The explicit UI states around remote data: loading,
success, empty, and error, often plus refreshing/stale.
Real networks fail and data can be absent; production
UI must communicate each state.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A delivery tracker should say "coming", "arrived",
"nothing ordered", or "delivery failed" - not stare
blankly.
R E A L E X A M P L E
if (loading) skeleton; if (error) retry UI; if
(!data.length) empty state; else list.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I model remote-data states explicitly so the UI never
confuses loading with empty or silently ignores failure.

Optimistic UI
I N O N E B R E AT H
Updating the interface immediately as if a mutation
will succeed, then confirming or rolling back based on
the server response. It removes perceived latency for
safe/reversible interactions.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You move the chess piece instantly, then the referee
confirms the move; if illegal, it snaps back.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Like button increments immediately; failed
request restores previous count and shows
feedback.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Optimistic UI improves responsiveness but needs
rollback, conflict handling, and care for irreversible or
high-risk operations.

entire application.

subtree. They do not catch every async/event error, so I
still handle those at their source. SECTION

R E L I A B I L I T Y, A R C H I T E C T U R E & D E L I V E RY
Retry
I N O N E B R E AT H
Attempting a failed operation again when the failure
may be temporary. Transient network/service errors
often succeed later.
M A K E I T S T I C K
If the vending machine says "network hiccup", try
once more; if it says "invalid coin", repeating 40
times is not intelligence.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Retry 503/timeouts; do not blindly retry a 400
validation error.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I retry only transient failures, cap attempts, make
operations idempotent where necessary, and combine
retries with backoff/jitter.

R E L I A B I L I T Y, A R C H I T E C T U R E & D E L I V E RY
Exponential backoff
I N O N E B R E AT H
A retry strategy where delays grow after consecutive
failures, often with random jitter. It gives a recovering
service breathing room and avoids synchronized retry
storms.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Knock again after 1s, then 2s, then 4s - do not
machine-gun the doorbell.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Retry delays 500ms, 1s, 2s, 4s plus random
jitter.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Exponential backoff reduces pressure during outages;
jitter prevents many clients from retrying in lockstep.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

R E L I A B I L I T Y, A R C H I T E C T U R E & D E L I V E RY
Idempotency
I N O N E B R E AT H
The property that repeating an operation has the same
intended effect as performing it once. Networks retry,
users double-click, and clients time out after servers
already committed work.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Pressing the elevator button 12 times should not
summon 12 elevators.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Payment request includes Idempotency-Key so a
retry returns the same payment instead of
charging twice.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Idempotency makes retries safe. I use idempotency keys
or natural resource semantics for operations that must
not duplicate side effects.

Message queue
I N O N E B R E AT H
A durable or buffered channel where producers
enqueue messages/jobs and consumers process
them later. It decouples request latency from
background work and smooths bursts.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Leave laundry tickets in a basket; workers take the
next ticket when ready.
R E A L E X A M P L E
API enqueues "send welcome email"; worker
consumes it asynchronously.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Queues decouple producers and consumers, buffer
load, and support retries; I design for at-least-once
delivery by making consumers idempotent.

segments.sectionTitle: I N O N E B R E AT H
segments.text: A durable or buffered channel where producers enqueue messages/jobs and consumers process them later. It decouples request latency from background work and smooths bursts.

segments.sectionTitle: S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
segments.text: Queues decouple producers and consumers, buffer load, and support retries; I design for at-least-once delivery by making consumers idempotent.

schedulers. I monitor failures, retry policy, poison jobs,
and idempotency.

An application deployed as one main unit, even if
internally modular. It minimizes distributed-system
complexity and can be the best architecture for many
teams.

Auth, users, payments, and notifications live in

A monolith is a deployment boundary, not necessarily a
code-quality problem. A modular monolith is often the
simplest scalable starting point.

R E L I A B I L I T Y, A R C H I T E C T U R E & D E L I V E RY
Microservices
I N O N E B R E AT H
An architecture where business capabilities are split
into independently deployable networked services. It
can enable independent scaling, ownership, and
deployment for sufficiently large systems/teams.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Instead of one restaurant, every station becomes a
separate restaurant and must phone the others.
Powerful, but now phones can fail.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Auth service, order service, billing service
each deploy and store data independently.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Microservices trade local code coupling for distributed-
system complexity. I introduce them when scaling,
ownership, or deployment boundaries justify that cost.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 147 / 310

I N O N E B R E AT H
Structuring code so different responsibilities live
behind appropriate boundaries. It reduces cognitive
load and makes change/testing safer.

Component renders UI; API module performs HTTP;
domain function computes business rule.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Separation of concerns gives modules focused reasons
to change. I avoid both giant components and pointless
abstraction layers.

Coupling
I N O N E B R E AT H
The degree to which one module depends on details
of another. High coupling makes changes ripple
unpredictably.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Two dancers glued together cannot change direction
independently.
R E A L E X A M P L E
UI imports database client directly: high
coupling; UI calls a small service interface:
lower coupling.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I aim for loose coupling through clear interfaces, while
accepting necessary coupling where the domain truly
connects things.

E2E tests cover critical journeys with high confidence

focused on valuable flows.

Mock
I N O N E B R E AT H
A test double that simulates a dependency and often
records interactions. Mocks isolate behavior and make
failures deterministic, but can hide integration problems.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A cardboard actor says the expected lines during
rehearsal, but that does not prove the real actor will
show up on opening night.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Mock payment client returns success; assert
service called charge with expected amount.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Mocks are useful at boundaries, but I avoid tests that
merely verify my mock setup instead of real behavior.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

N+1 query problem
I N O N E B R E AT H
A data-access pattern where one initial query is
followed by one additional query per returned item.
Query count grows linearly with result size and can
destroy latency.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Order 100 pizzas, but the kitchen sends a courier
back to the shop separately for each tomato.
R E A L E X A M P L E
SELECT users; then SELECT posts WHERE user_id=?
100 times. Replace with JOIN/batch/eager load.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
N+1 means 1 query to fetch parents plus N child queries.
I solve it with joins, batching, prefetch/eager loading, or
a data-loader pattern. SECTION

Big O notation
I N O N E B R E AT H
A way to describe how an algorithm's time or space
requirements grow as input size grows. It helps
compare scalability independent of a specific machine.
M A K E I T S T I C K
O(1) grabs one cookie; O(n) checks every cookie;
O(n^2) compares every cookie with every other
cookie because apparently we have lost control.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Array scan is O(n); nested pair comparison is
O(n^2); hash-map lookup is average O(1).
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Big O describes growth rate, not exact runtime. I use it to
reason about scalability while still profiling real code.

Array vs Set
I N O N E B R E AT H
Array is an ordered sequence with duplicates; Set
stores unique values with fast membership semantics.
Choosing the right collection can simplify logic and
improve lookup performance.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Guest list on paper vs a bouncer's unique stamp
registry.

selectedIds = new Set(); selectedIds.has(id)
avoids repeated array scans.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use arrays when order/indexing matter and Sets for
uniqueness or frequent membership checks.

Object vs Map
I N O N E B R E AT H
Objects are general JavaScript records; Map is a
dedicated key-value collection with arbitrary key
types and explicit iteration APIs. The choice affects
key semantics, iteration, and intent.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Object is a labeled cupboard built into the house;
Map is a purpose-built key locker.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const cache=new Map();
cache.set(userObject,result);
cache.get(userObject).
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use plain objects for record-like JSON-shaped data
and Map when I need dynamic keyed collections, non-
string keys, predictable iteration, or Map APIs.

Objects are general JavaScript records; Map is a dedicated key-value collection with arbitrary key types and explicit iteration APIs. The choice affects key semantics, iteration, and intent.

M A K E I T S T I C K

Object is a labeled cupboard built into the house; Map is a purpose-built key locker.

R E A L E X A M P L E

const cache=new Map();

cache.set(userObject,result); cache.get(userObject).

S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W

I use plain objects for record-like JSON-shaped data and Map when I need dynamic keyed collections, non-string keys, predictable iteration, or Map APIs.

Memory leak
I N O N E B R E AT H
Memory that remains reachable/retained even though
the application no longer needs it. Long-running apps
can become slower or crash as retained memory
accumulates.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You keep every takeaway container forever because
one tiny string is still tied to each box.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Forgotten event listener closes over a large
object after component cleanup should have
removed it.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
In garbage-collected JavaScript, leaks usually mean
unwanted references keep objects reachable. I
investigate heap growth, listeners, timers, caches, and
closures.

Automatic runtime reclamation of memory for objects
that are no longer reachable. JavaScript developers do
not manually free most memory, but must avoid
retaining unnecessary references.

eligible for collection.

Garbage collection reclaims unreachable memory
automatically; it does not prevent leaks caused by
objects that remain reachable accidentally.

even if contents are identical.

Technical debt
I N O N E B R E AT H
Future engineering cost created by shortcuts,
outdated design, or deliberate trade-offs in today's
implementation. Debt can accelerate delivery, but
unmanaged debt compounds and slows future change.

Ship a manual workflow for launch, document the
constraint, add telemetry, schedule replacement
when volume proves need.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Technical debt is not automatically bad. I make trade-
offs explicit, understand interest/risk, and prioritize
repayment based on product impact.

Type inference
I N O N E B R E AT H
TypeScript can often determine a value's type without
you writing it explicitly. It reduces noise while
preserving static checking.
M A K E I T S T I C K
If the waiter already sees you holding a coffee, you
do not need to label it “coffee” three times.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const count = 3; // inferred as number
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Type inference lets TypeScript derive types from values
and usage. I annotate public boundaries and complex
cases, but avoid redundant annotations.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not annotate everything just to “look typed”; let inference
work.

prove what the value is before using it.

never
I N O N E B R E AT H
A type representing values that should never occur. It
models impossible states and enables exhaustive
checks.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The “dragon enters payroll form” branch should be
impossible; never lets the compiler complain if it
becomes possible.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const exhaustive = (x: never) => x;
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
never represents an impossible value. I often use it in
exhaustive discriminated-union switches.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
If a new union member is added, an exhaustive check can
force every caller to handle it.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 189 / 310

Type narrowing
I N O N E B R E AT H
The process of refining a broad type into a more
specific one using runtime checks. It lets TypeScript
safely understand what operations are valid.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Security checks the costume at the door before
deciding whether you are the chef or the magician.
R E A L E X A M P L E
if (typeof value === "string")
value.toUpperCase();
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Narrowing uses control flow, typeof, in, instanceof, or
custom guards to move from broad types to precise
ones.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Narrow at boundaries rather than scattering unsafe casts.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 190 / 310

T Y P E S C R I P T: T H I N K I N G I N T Y P E S
Type guard
I N O N E B R E AT H
A runtime check that also teaches TypeScript a more
specific type. It centralizes validation and improves
downstream ergonomics.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A bouncer checks the wristband and announces
“yes, this is definitely VIP.”
R E A L E X A M P L E
function isUser(x: unknown): x is User
{ return !!x && typeof x === "object" && "id" in
x; }
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A type guard combines runtime validation with a type
predicate so the compiler can narrow values safely.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A guard is only trustworthy if the runtime check is actually
strong enough.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 191 / 310

T Y P E S C R I P T: T H I N K I N G I N T Y P E S
Discriminated union
I N O N E B R E AT H
A union whose members share a literal tag such as
status or type. It makes state machines and UI states
explicit and exhaustively checkable.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Every suitcase has a giant sticker: LOADING,
SUCCESS, or ERROR. No guessing what is inside.
R E A L E X A M P L E
type State = {status:"loading"}|
{status:"success";data:User[]}|
{status:"error";error:Error};
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Discriminated unions model mutually exclusive states
and let TypeScript narrow from a stable tag.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Excellent alternative to several booleans that can form
impossible combinations.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 192 / 310

T Y P E S C R I P T: T H I N K I N G I N T Y P E S
Structural typing
I N O N E B R E AT H
Type compatibility is based mainly on shape rather
than explicit inheritance names. It makes TypeScript
flexible with plain JavaScript objects.
M A K E I T S T I C K
If it has the right plug, voltage, and pins, TypeScript
cares less about the brand printed on the charger.
R E A L E X A M P L E
type Named={name:string}; const
x={name:"Ada",age:36}; const n:Named=x;
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
TypeScript is structurally typed: values are compatible
when their required shapes are compatible.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Useful flexibility, but accidental compatibility can happen with
very similar shapes.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 193 / 310

T Y P E S C R I P T: T H I N K I N G I N T Y P E S
keyof
I N O N E B R E AT H
A type operator that produces a union of the property
names of another type. It lets APIs accept only valid
keys.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Instead of letting someone request any drawer in the
universe, hand them the exact list of drawers in this
cabinet.
R E A L E X A M P L E
type UserKey = keyof User; // "id" | "name"
| ...
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
keyof turns object keys into a type-level union, which is
useful for safe property utilities and generic APIs.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Often paired with generics: K extends keyof T.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 194 / 310

T Y P E S C R I P T: T H I N K I N G I N T Y P E S
typeof in type space
I N O N E B R E AT H
TypeScript can derive a type from an existing
JavaScript value. It keeps runtime constants and
compile-time types synchronized.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Write the restaurant menu once; the waiter and
kitchen both read the same menu.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const config={mode:"prod",retries:3}; type

Mapped types iterate over keys at the type level to build
related object shapes.

Conditional type
I N O N E B R E AT H
A type-level if/else based on assignability. It enables
expressive generic transformations.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The type checker asks: “is this animal a duck? If yes,
give it pond rules; otherwise land rules.”
R E A L E X A M P L E
type IdOf<T> = T extends {id: infer I} ? I :
never;
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Conditional types select different result types based on
input types and are powerful in generic libraries.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Use sparingly; clever conditional types can become harder to
maintain than the code they protect.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 198 / 310

Generic constraint
I N O N E B R E AT H
A rule that limits what types a generic parameter may

capabilities.

Anyone can join the dance class, but everyone must

{ return x.id; }

Generic constraints let reusable code demand the
minimum shape it needs while preserving the caller's
more specific type.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Constrain to capabilities, not unnecessarily concrete types.

inference, which is ideal for configuration objects.

I N O N E B R E AT H
A developer instruction telling TypeScript to treat a
value as a particular type. Sometimes necessary at
trusted boundaries, but it does not perform runtime
validation.

Writing “definitely a tiger” on a cardboard box does
not make the animal inside a tiger.

HTMLDivElement;

A type assertion changes the compiler's view, not the
runtime value. I use it only when I have stronger
knowledge than the compiler.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Avoid using assertions to silence real uncertainty.

T Y P E S C R I P T: T H I N K I N G I N T Y P E S
Readonly
I N O N E B R E AT H
A type-level restriction preventing mutation through a
particular reference. It communicates intent and
reduces accidental state changes.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The museum gives you gloves and says: admire the
dinosaur, do not rearrange its bones.
R E A L E X A M P L E
function render(user: Readonly<User>) { /*
cannot assign user.name */ }
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Readonly expresses non-mutating contracts. It helps
document data flow but is not deep runtime immutability
by itself.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Readonly is compile-time protection, not Object.freeze.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 203 / 310

T Y P E S C R I P T: T H I N K I N G I N T Y P E S
Declaration file (.d.ts)
I N O N E B R E AT H
A file containing TypeScript type declarations without
runtime implementation. It describes JavaScript
libraries, globals, and module APIs to the compiler.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The .d.ts is the instruction manual; the JavaScript
package is the actual washing machine.
R E A L E X A M P L E
declare module "legacy-lib" { export function
parse(x:string): Result }
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Declaration files describe runtime APIs to TypeScript
and are how many JavaScript libraries become type-
safe to consume.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Types can be correct syntactically yet still lie about runtime
behavior.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 204 / 310

pages.canonicalText:
205
T Y P E S C R I P T: T H I N K I N G I N T Y P E S
Runtime validation vs
static types
I N O N E B R E AT H
TypeScript checks code before execution; runtime
validation checks real incoming values while the
program runs. External data can violate your TypeScript
declarations.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A blueprint says the bridge holds 10 tons; runtime
validation is weighing the truck before it drives on.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const json: unknown = await res.json();
validateUser(json);
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
TypeScript does not validate network data at runtime. I
validate untrusted boundaries and then narrow into
trusted domain types.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
This distinction is a frequent source of production bugs.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 205 / 310

206
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
State colocation
I N O N E B R E AT H
Keep state as close as possible to the components
that actually need it. It reduces unnecessary coupling
and rerenders.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Do not store your toothbrush in city hall because
three roommates might someday need it.
R E A L E X A M P L E
A modal's open state lives beside the modal
trigger, not in a global store.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I colocate state by default and lift or globalize it only
when multiple distant consumers truly share ownership.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Global state is convenient until every feature can mutate
everything.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 206 / 310

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Lifting state up
I N O N E B R E AT H
Move shared state to the nearest common owner of
components that need it. It creates one source of truth
for coordinated UI.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Two kids fighting over the thermostat need one
thermostat, not two fake thermostats.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Parent owns selectedId; sibling list sets it and
detail pane reads it.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I lift state to the lowest common ancestor when siblings
need coordinated access.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not lift farther than necessary.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 207 / 310

pages.canonicalText:
208
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Client state vs server
state
I N O N E B R E AT H
Client state is local UI/application state; server state is
remote data owned by the backend. They have
different lifecycles, freshness, caching, and
synchronization needs.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Your sticky-note “sidebar open” is yours; the bank
balance belongs to the bank.
R E A L E X A M P L E
useState for dialogOpen; query cache for GET /
users.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I separate client state from server state because remote
data needs fetching, caching, invalidation, retries, and
freshness semantics.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Treating API data like ordinary local state creates duplicated
synchronization logic.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 208 / 310

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
useReducer
I N O N E B R E AT H
A React hook that updates state by sending actions
through a reducer function. It helps when state
transitions are related or complex.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Instead of 12 people randomly moving chess pieces,
every move goes through one referee.
R E A L E X A M P L E
dispatch({type:"saveSucceeded", payload:user});
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use useReducer when several state fields change
together or when explicit state transitions improve
reasoning and testing.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
It is not automatically better than useState for simple state.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 209 / 310

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Reducer
I N O N E B R E AT H
A pure function that computes next state from current
state and an action. It centralizes transition rules.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The vending machine receives “COIN” and current
state, then deterministically decides the next state.
R E A L E X A M P L E
function reducer(state,action)
{ switch(action.type){...} }
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A reducer makes state transitions explicit and testable:
nextState = reducer(state, action).
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Keep reducers pure; side effects belong outside.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 210 / 310

Stale closure
I N O N E B R E AT H
A callback captures values from an older render and
later uses outdated data. It explains many timer, effect,
and async React bugs.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You text a friend directions from last Tuesday while
the restaurant moved yesterday.
R E A L E X A M P L E
setInterval(() => console.log(count),1000)
inside an effect with the wrong dependencies.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A stale closure happens when a callback closes over an
older render's values. I fix the ownership/dependency
model rather than blindly suppressing lint rules.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Functional state updates and refs solve some cases, but not
every stale-closure problem.

A browser API used to cancel fetches and other
abortable operations. It prevents unnecessary work
and stale responses from winning races.

You cancel the pizza order after realizing you
ordered it to your old apartment.

{signal:c.signal}); return ()=>c.abort();

I abort obsolete requests during cleanup when user
navigation or rapidly changing inputs can make previous
work irrelevant.

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Async request race
I N O N E B R E AT H
Two requests overlap and an older response arrives
after a newer one, overwriting fresh UI. Fast typing,
route changes, and filters can create incorrect data
even when every request succeeds.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You ask “weather Berlin?” then “weather Rome?”;
Berlin answers last and your Rome screen shows
Berlin rain.
R E A L E X A M P L E
query A starts, query B starts, B returns, A
returns -> stale overwrite.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I guard async races by cancellation, request identity, or
a server-state library that tracks query keys and
staleness.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
“Last response wins” is not always “latest intent wins.”
Explain it aloud before swiping. 213 / 310

Component composition

Build larger UI by combining focused components
instead of adding endless configuration flags to one
component. It keeps APIs flexible and reduces giant
conditional components.

LEGO bricks compose better than one 900-button
“universal brick.”

I prefer composition when consumers need flexible
structure; it often scales better than a component with
dozens of boolean props.

Too many tiny wrappers can also obscure the UI; use
meaningful boundaries.

Transition
I N O N E B R E AT H
A lower-priority React update that can be interrupted
so urgent interactions stay responsive. It helps
expensive non-urgent UI updates avoid blocking typing/
click feedback.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The cashier serves the person at the desk before
reorganizing the entire cereal aisle.
R E A L E X A M P L E
startTransition(()=>setFilter(next));
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Transitions mark updates as non-urgent so React can
prioritize immediate interactions and keep the interface
responsive.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A transition does not make expensive computation free; profile
real bottlenecks.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 219 / 310

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
useDeferredValue
I N O N E B R E AT H
Lets a derived part of UI lag behind an urgent value
temporarily. It keeps input responsive when
downstream rendering is expensive.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Your mouth says the new word instantly; the giant
scoreboard updates a moment later.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const deferredQuery = useDeferredValue(query);
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
useDeferredValue lets non-urgent rendering trail an
urgent value, which can improve responsiveness for
expensive result views.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Debouncing changes when work begins; deferring changes
rendering priority - not the same thing.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 220 / 310

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Memoization boundary
I N O N E B R E AT H
A deliberate place where stable inputs can allow
expensive work or child rendering to be reused. It can
reduce repeated computation, but adds complexity and
comparison overhead.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You laminate a frequently used map instead of
redrawing Europe every time someone asks where
France is.
R E A L E X A M P L E
React.memo(Chart), useMemo(expensiveProjection)
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I memoize after identifying a meaningful cost and stable
inputs, rather than wrapping every function and
component by habit.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Incorrect dependencies can create stale results; unnecessary
memoization can make code worse.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 221 / 310

Referential stability
I N O N E B R E AT H
Whether the same object/function reference is
preserved across renders. React memoization and
effect dependencies often use reference identity.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Two identical-looking hotel keys are still different
physical keys.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const options = useMemo(()=>({limit:20}),[]);
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Referential stability matters when consumers compare
by identity, such as memoized children or effect
dependencies.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not stabilize references unless identity actually matters.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 222 / 310

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Render purity
I N O N E B R E AT H
A React render should calculate UI from inputs without
causing external side effects. Pure rendering lets
React safely rerun, pause, or discard work.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A restaurant menu printer may print the menu twice;
it must not charge your card each time it prints.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Do not call fetch-and-write or localStorage
mutation directly during render.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
React rendering should be pure: same props/state/
context should describe the same UI without external
mutations.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Development behaviors may intentionally render more than
once to expose impurity.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 224 / 310

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Error recovery boundary
I N O N E B R E AT H
A UI boundary designed not just to show an error but
to offer a meaningful recovery path. Production UX
should degrade locally rather than turning the whole
page into a dead end.
M A K E I T S T I C K
If the toaster breaks, you replace breakfast - you do
not evacuate the entire house.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Widget error -> retry button; editor error ->
preserve draft and reload component.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I place error boundaries around meaningful failure
domains and design recovery, telemetry, and preserved
user work where possible.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
An error boundary does not catch every async/event-handler
error automatically.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 226 / 310

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Feature boundary
I N O N E B R E AT H
A module/component boundary aligned with a user-
facing capability rather than file type alone. It
improves ownership and keeps related UI, hooks, tests,
and data logic close.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Keep everything for “pizza delivery” in one kitchen
station instead of putting every spoon in one building
and every plate in another.
R E A L E X A M P L E
features/search/{SearchBox, useSearch, api,
tests}
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Feature-oriented boundaries often scale better than
giant global folders like components/, hooks/, utils/
when product complexity grows.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Shared primitives should remain genuinely shared, not become
a dumping ground.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 227 / 310

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Presentational vs
orchestration logic
I N O N E B R E AT H
Separate UI rendering from workflow/data
coordination when that separation clarifies
responsibilities. It makes complex screens easier to
test and redesign.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The waiter handles the table; the kitchen coordinates
cooking. One person can do both in a tiny cafe, but
not always at scale.
R E A L E X A M P L E
SearchPage orchestrates query/state; ResultsList
renders rows.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I separate orchestration from presentation when it
reduces coupling, while avoiding rigid “container/
component” ceremony for simple cases.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
The boundary is a tool, not a mandatory folder pattern.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 228 / 310

229
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Optimistic concurrency in
UI
I N O N E B R E AT H
Allow local interaction immediately, then reconcile
with authoritative server state and version/conflict
rules. It makes collaborative or latency-sensitive UIs
feel fast without pretending conflicts cannot happen.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You pencil your name into the booking sheet, then
the receptionist confirms whether someone else
took the slot first.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Update UI -> send mutation with version ->
accept or rollback/conflict message.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Optimistic UI is strongest when paired with backend
concurrency guarantees and a clear rollback/conflict
strategy.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A pretty optimistic animation cannot fix duplicate writes or lost
updates on the server.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 229 / 310

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Accessibility state
I N O N E B R E AT H
Interactive components must expose their current
state to assistive technologies, not only visually. A
screen reader needs to know expanded, selected,
invalid, busy, and disabled states.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A traffic light that changes color but never tells a
blind pedestrian anything is incomplete.
R E A L E X A M P L E
aria-expanded={open}, aria-invalid={hasError},
native disabled
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I treat accessibility semantics as part of component
state, not decorative metadata added at the end.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Prefer native controls because they carry much of this
behavior automatically.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 230 / 310

M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Module
I N O N E B R E AT H
A cohesive unit that exposes a public interface while
hiding internal implementation details. Modules
reduce the amount of code a developer must
understand at once.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A microwave has buttons on the front; you do not
need its wiring diagram to heat soup.
R E A L E X A M P L E
payments/index.ts exports charge(); internal
gateway mapping stays private.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A good module has a focused responsibility, a small
public surface, and internals that can change without
breaking callers.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A folder is not automatically a module; the dependency
boundary matters.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 231 / 310

M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Encapsulation
I N O N E B R E AT H
Hide internal state/implementation and expose only
the operations consumers need. It prevents distant
code from depending on fragile details.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You drive using steering wheel and pedals, not by
reaching into the gearbox with your hand.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Cart exposes addItem(); callers do not mutate
cart.items internals directly.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Encapsulation protects invariants by controlling how
state and behavior are accessed.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Getters for every private field are not meaningful encapsulation
if callers still control everything.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 232 / 310

M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Abstraction
I N O N E B R E AT H
A simplified model/interface that hides irrelevant
detail for a particular task. It lets callers reason at the

M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Dependency inversion
I N O N E B R E AT H
High-level business logic depends on abstractions/
capabilities rather than concrete infrastructure
details. It reduces coupling to databases, vendors, and
frameworks.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The lamp depends on “electricity from a socket,” not
“this exact power station turbine #7.”
R E A L E X A M P L E
CheckoutService accepts PaymentGateway
interface; Stripe adapter implements it.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Dependency inversion keeps domain policy independent
from replaceable infrastructure by depending on stable
interfaces.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not invent interfaces for every class; use them where
volatility or testing justifies the seam.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 235 / 310

Ports and adapters
I N O N E B R E AT H
Architecture where core logic exposes/consumes
ports and external systems connect through adapters.
It keeps domain behavior testable and independent
from UI/database/vendor details.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The castle has standardized gates; horses, cars, and
delivery robots can each use an adapter to enter.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Domain -> PaymentPort; StripePaymentAdapter ->
Stripe SDK.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Ports-and-adapters isolates core use cases from
infrastructure and makes external integrations
replaceable.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Useful when domain logic matters; excessive ceremony is
wasteful for tiny CRUD apps.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 236 / 310

Layered architecture
I N O N E B R E AT H
Organize responsibilities into layers such as
presentation, application, domain, and infrastructure.
It creates dependency direction and reduces cross-
cutting spaghetti.

Guests talk to the waiter, waiter to kitchen; guests do

responsibility and dependencies mostly flow inward/
downward.

Avoid pass-through layers that add files but no semantic value.

M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Pure core, imperative
shell
I N O N E B R E AT H
Keep business rules pure where possible and put I/O/
side effects at the edges. It makes critical logic
deterministic and easy to test.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Do the math on paper first; only then call the bank,
printer, and email robot.
R E A L E X A M P L E
calculateQuote(input) is pure; handler fetches
DB data and sends result.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I isolate side effects at boundaries and keep core
decision logic pure when practical.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Not every application needs a perfectly pure domain; optimize
for clarity.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 238 / 310

M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Single Responsibility
Principle
I N O N E B R E AT H
A module should have one coherent reason to change.
It prevents unrelated concerns from becoming
entangled.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A Swiss Army knife is useful; a Swiss Army
refrigerator-toaster-tax-accountant is not.
R E A L E X A M P L E
InvoiceCalculator calculates totals; EmailSender
sends invoices.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
SRP is about reasons to change, not making every
function microscopic.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Over-splitting can create navigation overhead and weak
abstractions.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 239 / 310

M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Open/Closed Principle
I N O N E B R E AT H
Prefer designs that allow new behavior through
extension without repeatedly modifying fragile central
logic. It can reduce regression risk in frequently
extended systems.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Add a new train carriage instead of welding a new
room into the locomotive engine each week.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Renderer registry maps type -> renderer instead
of a 500-line switch edited by every feature.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use extension points where variation is proven and
frequent; I do not pre-build plugin systems for
hypothetical needs.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
YAGNI still applies.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 240 / 310

Adapter pattern
I N O N E B R E AT H
Wrap an incompatible or vendor-specific interface
behind the interface your application wants. It
contains third-party churn and translation logic.
M A K E I T S T I C K

Adapters translate between boundaries and keep
vendor-specific details from leaking through the
codebase.

An adapter should simplify the boundary, not merely rename
every method one-to-one.

M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Repository pattern
I N O N E B R E AT H
An abstraction representing access to domain data
without exposing persistence mechanics to callers. It
can isolate SQL/ORM details from use cases.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The librarian fetches books; you ask for ISBN 123,
not “walk to shelf row 8 and run SQL.”
R E A L E X A M P L E
UserRepository.findById(id) -> User | null.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A repository can separate domain/application logic from
persistence details, especially when queries and
invariants deserve a stable interface.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not add repositories that are just thin copies of an ORM with
no value.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 242 / 310

M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Code smell
I N O N E B R E AT H
A symptom suggesting design trouble, not proof of a
bug. Smells guide investigation and refactoring.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Smoke does not always mean the house is burning,
but you should probably look.
R E A L E X A M P L E
12 boolean props, 900-line component, duplicated
conditional business rules.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Code smells are heuristics. I use them to ask why code
is hard to change rather than applying automatic “clean
code” rules.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Context matters: long code can be clearer than a premature
abstraction.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 243 / 310

244
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Refactoring
I N O N E B R E AT H
Change internal structure while preserving externally
observable behavior. It improves design safely when
backed by tests and small steps.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Reorganize the kitchen cabinets without changing
tonight's menu.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Extract pricing rule, rename types, split
module; tests keep behavior stable.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Refactoring improves structure without intentionally
changing behavior. I prefer incremental, test-backed
changes over big rewrites.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A rewrite is not the same as a refactor.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 244 / 310

M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Feature flag
I N O N E B R E AT H
A runtime or deployment control that enables behavior
for selected users/environments. It decouples code
deployment from feature release and supports safer
rollout.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The roller coaster is built, but only staff with the
green wristband may ride it today.
R E A L E X A M P L E
if (flags.newCheckout) return <NewCheckout/>;
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Feature flags support gradual rollout and fast
disablement, but need ownership and cleanup because
stale flags become permanent branches.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Never rely on a frontend flag as an authorization boundary.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 245 / 310

pages.canonicalText:
246
DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Normalization
I N O N E B R E AT H
Structure relational data to reduce duplication and
update anomalies, usually by separating distinct
entities. It improves consistency and makes one fact
have one authoritative home.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Do not write Grandma's phone number on 40 recipe
cards; keep one contact record and reference it.
R E A L E X A M P L E
orders.user_id -> users.id instead of copying
user email/address everywhere.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Normalization reduces duplicated facts and anomalies; I
denormalize selectively when measured read patterns
justify it.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Over-normalization can make read paths unnecessarily
complex.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 246 / 310
