pages.canonicalText:
247
DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Denormalization
I N O N E B R E AT H
Intentionally duplicate or precompute data to make
reads simpler or faster. It trades write complexity/
storage for read performance.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Keep a snack in every room so you do not walk to
the kitchen, but now every room needs restocking.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Store order_total on order instead of
recalculating from line items for every list
view.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Denormalization is a deliberate performance trade-off; I
define how duplicated data stays consistent.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
If you cannot explain the synchronization rule, the duplicate
may become corruption.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 247 / 310

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Database constraint
I N O N E B R E AT H
A rule enforced by the database, such as NOT NULL,
CHECK, UNIQUE, or FOREIGN KEY. It protects
invariants even when multiple application paths write
data.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The nightclub door physically rejects anyone without
a valid ticket; it does not trust every promoter to
remember the rule.
R E A L E X A M P L E
UNIQUE(email), CHECK(quantity > 0), FOREIGN KEY
user_id.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I enforce critical data invariants in the database as well
as validating in the application.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Application validation gives nicer UX; database constraints give
authoritative protection.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 248 / 310

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Unique constraint
I N O N E B R E AT H
Guarantees that a value or combination of values
cannot appear more than once. It closes race
conditions that “check then insert” application logic
cannot safely prevent alone.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Two people race for username “wizard”; the
database is the final referee.
R E A L E X A M P L E
UNIQUE(tenant_id, slug)
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A unique constraint is the authoritative way to enforce
uniqueness under concurrency.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Catch and translate the constraint error into a useful domain
response.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 249 / 310

Composite index
I N O N E B R E AT H
An index built on multiple columns in a defined order.
It can optimize queries filtering/sorting by those
columns together.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A phone book sorted by country then surname is
great for “Germany + Müller” but not every possible
lookup.
R E A L E X A M P L E
INDEX(tenant_id, created_at DESC)
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Composite index column order should match important
query predicates/sorts; I verify with query plans rather
than guessing.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
More indexes increase write cost and storage.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 250 / 310

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Query plan
I N O N E B R E AT H
The database's chosen strategy for executing a
query. It reveals whether indexes, scans, joins, and
estimates behave as expected.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You ask for a route; the query plan is the GPS
showing whether it takes the motorway or walks
through a swamp.
R E A L E X A M P L E
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT ...
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I inspect query plans for slow queries to see actual
scans, join strategies, row estimates, and index usage.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
“There is an index” does not mean the optimizer will use it.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 251 / 310

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Schema migration
I N O N E B R E AT H
A controlled change to database structure or data as
the application evolves. Production databases must
change without losing data or breaking old/new app
versions.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Renovate a hotel while guests are still sleeping
inside.
R E A L E X A M P L E
add nullable column -> deploy code -> backfill
-> enforce NOT NULL later.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I design migrations for compatibility and rollback/
forward recovery, especially when deployments overlap
versions.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Large locks and table rewrites can turn a harmless-looking
migration into an outage.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 252 / 310

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Connection pool
I N O N E B R E AT H
A managed set of reusable database connections
shared by application requests. Opening a new DB
connection per request is expensive and databases
have finite connection capacity.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Keep 20 taxis ready instead of manufacturing a new
car for every passenger.
R E A L E X A M P L E
API process borrows a connection, runs query/
transaction, returns it to pool.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Connection pools amortize connection setup and cap
concurrency, but pool size must respect total database
capacity across app instances.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
100 app replicas x 50 connections can overwhelm a DB that
supports 300.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 253 / 310

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Isolation level
I N O N E B R E AT H
A transaction setting controlling which effects of
concurrent transactions may be observed. It balances
correctness guarantees against concurrency/
performance.
M A K E I T S T I C K
How much can two accountants see of each other's
half-finished spreadsheets?
R E A L E X A M P L E
READ COMMITTED vs REPEATABLE READ vs
SERIALIZABLE.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Isolation levels define allowed concurrency phenomena.
I choose based on the invariant rather than defaulting to
the strongest level everywhere.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Database implementations differ in exact semantics; know your
engine.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 254 / 310

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Deadlock
I N O N E B R E AT H
Two transactions each hold resources the other
needs, so neither can proceed. Concurrent locking can
create circular waits.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Two people in a narrow hallway each refuse to step
backward.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Tx A locks row 1 then wants 2; Tx B locks row 2
then wants 1.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Databases detect deadlocks and abort a participant; I
keep transactions short, lock in consistent order, and
retry safe failures.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Deadlock retries require idempotent transaction behavior.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 255 / 310

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Pessimistic locking
I N O N E B R E AT H
Lock data before modifying it so competitors must
wait. Useful when conflicts are likely and the cost of
concurrent changes is high.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Put a “DO NOT TOUCH - I'M EDITING” sign on the
only whiteboard.
R E A L E X A M P L E
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a transaction.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Pessimistic locking serializes access to contested data,
trading throughput for stronger coordination.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Long user-driven transactions holding DB locks are usually
dangerous.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 256 / 310

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
MVCC
I N O N E B R E AT H
Multi-Version Concurrency Control keeps multiple row
versions so reads and writes can coexist with less
blocking. It is a core reason modern relational
databases can support concurrent transactions
efficiently.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Readers get yesterday's newspaper copy while the
editor prepares today's edition.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Postgres snapshots let readers see a consistent
version while another transaction writes.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
MVCC uses row versions and transaction snapshots to
provide isolation with reduced read/write blocking.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Old versions still require cleanup; long transactions can create
bloat.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 257 / 310

Read replica
I N O N E B R E AT H
A copy of a primary database used mainly to serve
reads. It can scale read-heavy workloads and isolate
analytics/reporting traffic.
M A K E I T S T I C K
One chef writes the master recipe; many
photocopies let 100 students read it.
R E A L E X A M P L E
writes -> primary; product browse reads ->
replica.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Read replicas scale reads but introduce replication lag,
so read-after-write consistency may need routing to
primary.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Never assume a replica is instantly current.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 258 / 310

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N
Sharding
I N O N E B R E AT H
Partition a dataset across multiple database nodes
using a shard key. It can scale storage/write throughput
beyond one machine.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Instead of one giant library, surnames A-M go to
building 1 and N-Z to building 2.
R E A L E X A M P L E
tenant_id hash decides database shard.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Sharding distributes data and load, but makes cross-
shard queries, transactions, rebalancing, and operations
substantially harder.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Choose a shard key based on access patterns and hotspot
risk.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 259 / 310

ORM
I N O N E B R E AT H
A library that maps application objects/models to
database operations. It can speed development,
parameterize queries, and centralize schema access.

An interpreter translates your app's sentences into
SQL, but sometimes misunderstands poetry.

ORMs improve productivity, but I still understand the
SQL, indexes, transaction semantics, and query count
they produce.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
The N+1 problem often hides behind convenient ORM property
access.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 260 / 310

CAC H I N G , P E R F O R M A N C E & S CA L A B I L I T Y
Cache-aside
I N O N E B R E AT H
The application checks cache first, loads from source
on miss, then populates the cache. It is simple and
common for read-heavy data.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Check the fridge; if milk is missing, go to the shop
and put the new milk in the fridge.
R E A L E X A M P L E
cache.get(key) -> miss -> db.query ->
cache.set(key,value,ttl).
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Cache-aside keeps the database authoritative while
lazily populating cache on demand.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Plan for stale data, stampedes, and what happens when cache
is unavailable.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 261 / 310

CAC H I N G , P E R F O R M A N C E & S CA L A B I L I T Y
Write-through cache
I N O N E B R E AT H
Writes update the cache and backing store as part of
the write path. It keeps cached values fresh for
subsequent reads.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Every time the restaurant changes the menu, both
the kitchen board and website are updated before
saying “done.”
R E A L E X A M P L E
save user -> DB + cache before acknowledging.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Write-through improves cache freshness but increases
write-path latency and couples availability to both
systems unless carefully designed.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Failure ordering matters: which write succeeds first?
Explain it aloud before swiping. 262 / 310

CAC H I N G , P E R F O R M A N C E & S CA L A B I L I T Y
Write-behind cache
I N O N E B R E AT H
Writes are accepted into cache/buffer and persisted
to the backing store asynchronously. It can absorb
bursts and reduce perceived write latency.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Drop letters into a mailbox now; the postal truck
takes them to headquarters later.
R E A L E X A M P L E
counter increments in cache; worker flushes
batches to durable store.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Write-behind can improve throughput but introduces
durability and consistency risk if buffered writes are lost.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Use only when the data-loss window and recovery model are
acceptable.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 263 / 310

CAC H I N G , P E R F O R M A N C E & S CA L A B I L I T Y
Eviction policy
I N O N E B R E AT H
The rule deciding what cached item to remove when
capacity is full. Caches are finite; retaining the wrong
entries lowers usefulness.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Your tiny fridge must decide whether to throw away
the week-old celery or today's cake.
R E A L E X A M P L E
LRU removes least-recently-used entries.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Eviction policy should match workload locality; LRU is
common but not universally optimal.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Eviction is different from TTL expiration.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 264 / 310

locality: recently used items are often reused soon.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The least-used mug gets kicked out of the cupboard
when a new mug arrives.

Map + doubly-linked list can implement O(1) get/
put LRU.

LRU prioritizes recently accessed data and is a common
bounded-cache policy.

A scan through millions of one-off items can pollute an LRU
cache.

Cache stampede
I N O N E B R E AT H
Many requests miss or expire the same hot key and all
hit the origin simultaneously. A cache can accidentally
amplify load exactly when protection is needed.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The snack shelf empties and 500 employees all drive
to the same supermarket at once.
R E A L E X A M P L E
hot key expires -> 10k requests -> 10k DB
queries.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I mitigate stampedes with request coalescing/locks,
jittered TTLs, early refresh, or stale-while-revalidate.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Long identical TTLs make synchronized expiry more likely.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 266 / 310

CAC H I N G , P E R F O R M A N C E & S CA L A B I L I T Y
Stale-while-revalidate
I N O N E B R E AT H
Serve slightly stale cached data immediately while
refreshing it in the background. It trades bounded
freshness for low latency and resilience.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Serve yesterday's menu for 20 seconds while the
waiter fetches today's menu, instead of making
everyone stand outside.
R E A L E X A M P L E
CDN/browser returns stale response and
revalidates asynchronously.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Stale-while-revalidate is useful when bounded staleness
is acceptable and fast availability matters more than
instant freshness.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not use for data where stale values can cause unsafe
decisions.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 267 / 310

bandwidth when cached representations are

Conditional request
I N O N E B R E AT H
An HTTP request that asks the server to send content
only if a condition about cached state is met. It saves
bandwidth and work while preserving freshness
checks.
M A K E I T S T I C K
“Bring me the newspaper only if it changed since my
copy.”
R E A L E X A M P L E
If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since -> 304.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Conditional requests combine caching with validation so
clients can reuse local content safely when unchanged.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A 304 saves payload bytes but still incurs a network round trip.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 269 / 310

Distributed cache
I N O N E B R E AT H
A cache shared across application instances,
commonly over the network. It gives multiple servers a
common cache instead of isolated in-process copies.
M A K E I T S T I C K
All restaurant branches share one giant pantry
inventory system instead of each guessing what
exists.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Redis used by 20 API replicas.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A distributed cache improves sharing and capacity but
adds network latency, serialization, failure modes, and
consistency concerns.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not put every read behind Redis by reflex; local caching can
be much cheaper for some data.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 270 / 310

Circuit breaker
I N O N E B R E AT H
Stop calling a failing dependency temporarily after a
failure threshold, then probe recovery. It prevents
repeated slow failures from consuming all resources.
M A K E I T S T I C K
If the elevator is broken, stop sending 200 people to
press the button every second.
R E A L E X A M P L E
CLOSED -> failures -> OPEN -> timeout ->
HALF_OPEN probe.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Circuit breakers fail fast when a dependency is
unhealthy and give it time to recover.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
They require sensible fallbacks/errors; “open” is still a failure
from the user's perspective.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 271 / 310

Backpressure
I N O N E B R E AT H
A mechanism that slows producers when consumers
cannot keep up. Without it, queues/memory grow until
latency explodes or the system crashes.
M A K E I T S T I C K
If the sink drains one bucket per minute, stop
opening ten fire hoses into it.
R E A L E X A M P L E
stream pauses reads; queue rejects/throttles
producers above capacity.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Backpressure matches production rate to downstream
capacity and is essential for stable streaming and queue
systems.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Unbounded queues are delayed outages.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 272 / 310

consume everything. It limits blast radius.

dependency or workload from exhausting the whole
service.

Autoscaling
I N O N E B R E AT H
Automatically change compute capacity based on
demand or schedules. It handles variable load without
permanently paying for peak capacity.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Open more supermarket checkouts when the queue
grows, close them when the store empties.

replicas scale on CPU, queue depth, or request
concurrency.

Autoscaling adds capacity reactively, but metrics,
startup time, database limits, and traffic spikes still
matter.

Scaling stateless app replicas does not scale a saturated
database automatically.

CAC H I N G , P E R F O R M A N C E & S CA L A B I L I T Y
Capacity planning
I N O N E B R E AT H
Estimate how much traffic, storage, concurrency, and
failure headroom the system can support. Scalability is
an engineering budget, not a magic architecture label.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Know how many pizzas your ovens can bake before
inviting 10,000 people to dinner.
R E A L E X A M P L E
benchmark 500 req/s per instance; plan replicas
+ 30% headroom.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Capacity planning combines measured service limits,
expected growth, peak patterns, and safety margin so
bottlenecks are found before production.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Use load tests and real telemetry; guesses age badly.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 275 / 310

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
Large Language Model (LLM)
I N O N E B R E AT H
A neural network trained to predict and generate
sequences of tokens from context. LLMs power chat,
extraction, coding, summarization, classification, and
tool-using systems.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A supercharged autocomplete read an enormous
library and became weirdly good at continuing useful
patterns.
R E A L E X A M P L E
prompt tokens -> model inference -> generated
tokens.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
An LLM models token probabilities conditioned on
context; product quality depends on prompting,
grounding, tools, evaluation, and system design around
the model.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Fluent output is not proof of factual correctness.

affects context usage, throughput, and billing.

Context window
I N O N E B R E AT H
The maximum amount of token context a model can
attend to in one request/session window. It limits how
much conversation, documents, and tool output can be
considered at once.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Your desk can hold 50 pages; page 51 means
removing or compressing something.
R E A L E X A M P L E
system + history + retrieved docs + user prompt
+ output budget must fit.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
The context window is finite, so I budget high-value
context, summarize history, and retrieve relevant
evidence rather than dumping everything.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A huge context window does not guarantee the model uses
every token equally well.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 279 / 310

Embedding
I N O N E B R E AT H
A numeric vector representing semantic properties of
content. Embeddings enable similarity search,
clustering, recommendations, and retrieval.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Words become coordinates on a giant meaning map;
“puppy” lands closer to “dog” than “database.”
R E A L E X A M P L E
embed(query) -> vector; compare cosine

RAG
I N O N E B R E AT H
Retrieval-Augmented Generation: retrieve external
evidence and give it to the model before generation. It
grounds answers in current/private knowledge without
retraining the model.

open exactly three relevant encyclopedia pages.

question -> retrieve chunks -> prompt with

RAG separates knowledge retrieval from generation.

prompt design, and evaluation.

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
Chunking
I N O N E B R E AT H
Split documents into retrieval-sized pieces, usually
with boundaries/overlap/metadata. Retrieval works
better when chunks are coherent and small enough to
target precisely.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Do not store an entire cookbook as one index card;
split by recipe, not random every 400 characters.
R E A L E X A M P L E
heading-aware chunks with document ID and
section metadata.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Chunking is a retrieval design decision: I preserve
semantic boundaries and test chunk size/overlap
against real queries.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Too small loses context; too large dilutes relevance and
consumes tokens.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 284 / 310

Grounding
I N O N E B R E AT H
Constrain or support model output with authoritative
evidence, tools, or state. It reduces unsupported
invention and makes outputs verifiable.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The model must answer while keeping one hand on
the source document.
R E A L E X A M P L E
answer only from retrieved policy + return
source IDs.

Grounding ties generation to external truth sources; I
design the UI and evals so unsupported claims are
detectable.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Grounding reduces hallucination risk; it does not eliminate it.

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
Hallucination
I N O N E B R E AT H
A model produces plausible-looking output that is
unsupported or incorrect. LLMs optimize generation
probabilities, not guaranteed truth.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A confident tour guide invents a castle because the
story sounds right.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Model invents an API method that does not exist.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Hallucination is unsupported generation. I mitigate it with
grounding, constrained outputs, tool verification,
abstention, and task-specific evals.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not solve high-stakes hallucination only with “be accurate”
in the prompt.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 287 / 310

Prompt injection

Untrusted content attempts to manipulate model

R E A L E X A M P L E

instructions and send secrets.”
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
Tool calling
I N O N E B R E AT H
A model selects a structured tool/function and
arguments so software can perform external actions
or fetch data. It connects probabilistic language
understanding to deterministic capabilities.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The model is the receptionist; tools are the actual
locksmith, calculator, and database clerk.
R E A L E X A M P L E
model -> {tool:"getWeather", args:
{city:"Berlin"}} -> app executes -> result ->
model.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Tool calling lets the model choose structured operations,
but the application must validate arguments, enforce
authorization, and control side effects.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
The model choosing a tool is not permission to execute it
blindly.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 289 / 310

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
Agent loop
I N O N E B R E AT H
A repeated cycle where a model observes state,
chooses an action/tool, receives results, and
continues until done. It supports multi-step tasks that
require planning and external operations.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Think → use screwdriver → look again → use wrench
→ check result.
R E A L E X A M P L E
observe -> model -> tool -> observation -> model
-> final.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
An agent is usually a control loop around a model and
tools. I bound steps, permissions, budgets, and
termination conditions.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
More autonomy means more failure surface; use the simplest
workflow that works.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 291 / 310

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
Model routing
I N O N E B R E AT H
Choose among models based on task, quality need,
latency, availability, or cost. Not every request needs
the largest model.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Use a bicycle for the corner shop and a truck for
moving a piano.
R E A L E X A M P L E
classifier -> cheap model for extraction;
stronger model for complex reasoning; fallback
on outage.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Model routing optimizes quality/cost/latency by
matching model capability to task and providing fallback
paths.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Routing itself needs evals; a bad router can erase savings or
quality.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 292 / 310

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
Temperature
I N O N E B R E AT H
A sampling parameter influencing randomness in
token selection. It changes diversity, not the model's
underlying knowledge.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Low temperature orders the usual pizza; high
temperature may add pineapple, mango, and
existentialism.
R E A L E X A M P L E
temperature near 0 for deterministic extraction;
higher for brainstorming.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Temperature controls sampling randomness. I keep it
low for constrained factual tasks and only raise it when
diversity is useful.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Temperature is not a “creativity intelligence” knob and cannot
fix poor grounding.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 293 / 310

separately from total generation time and tokens per

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
KV cache
I N O N E B R E AT H
Inference memory storing attention key/value states
for previously processed tokens so they do not need
full recomputation during autoregressive generation.
It makes token-by-token generation dramatically more
efficient.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The model keeps notes from pages 1-100 instead of
rereading the entire book before writing every next
word.
R E A L E X A M P L E
prompt prefill builds KV states; each new token
reuses prior states.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
KV cache reduces repeated attention computation
during generation but consumes significant memory that
grows with sequence length and concurrency.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not confuse runtime KV cache with application-level
response caching.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 297 / 310

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
Prefix / prompt caching
I N O N E B R E AT H
Reuse computation or results for identical/repeated
prompt prefixes across requests when supported.
Long shared system prompts or documents can
otherwise be reprocessed repeatedly.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A professor remembers the 40-page exam
instructions and only rereads each student's unique
question.
R E A L E X A M P L E
shared 8k-token system prefix reused across many
requests.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Prompt/prefix caching can reduce latency and compute
for repeated context, but hit conditions and cache
semantics are provider/runtime-specific.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Measure actual hit rates and cost savings; do not assume a
cache exists just because prompts look similar.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 298 / 310

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
Quantization
I N O N E B R E AT H
Represent model weights/activations with lower
numerical precision. It reduces memory and can
improve inference speed, sometimes with quality trade-
offs.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Store prices to fewer decimal places so the
notebook gets much smaller, while trying not to ruin
the accounting.
R E A L E X A M P L E
16-bit weights -> 8-bit or 4-bit representation.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Quantization compresses model representation for
cheaper/faster inference; I validate task quality because
lower precision can change outputs.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Memory savings do not translate identically to speed on every
hardware/runtime.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 299 / 310

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S
AI evaluation (eval)
I N O N E B R E AT H
A repeatable test set and scoring process for
measuring model/system behavior on representative
tasks. AI outputs are probabilistic; intuition and a few
demos are not enough for reliable iteration.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Do not judge a goalkeeper from three Instagram
clips; run 500 representative shots and score them.
R E A L E X A M P L E
dataset of prompts + expected properties ->
automated/semantic/human scoring -> regression
gates.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Evals are tests for AI behavior. I build task-specific
datasets, measure quality dimensions, and run
regressions whenever prompts/models/retrieval change.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A single aggregate score can hide catastrophic failures in
important slices.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 300 / 310

T E S T I N G , S E C U R I T Y & O P E R AT I O N A L E XC E L L E N C E
Test pyramid
I N O N E B R E AT H
A heuristic favoring many fast focused tests, fewer
integration tests, and a smaller number of expensive
E2E tests. It balances confidence, speed, and
maintainability.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Use many smoke detectors, some fire drills, and a
few full city evacuation exercises.
R E A L E X A M P L E
hundreds unit/component + dozens integration +
critical-path E2E.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
The pyramid is a cost heuristic, not a quota. I put
behavior at the cheapest layer that gives meaningful
confidence.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Frontend-heavy products may use a testing trophy shape;
focus on confidence per cost, not ideology.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 301 / 310

Contract test
I N O N E B R E AT H
Verifies that two services/components agree on their
integration contract. It catches breaking API changes
without requiring a full end-to-end environment.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The plug manufacturer and socket manufacturer test
the shared standard separately.
R E A L E X A M P L E
consumer expects {id,name}; provider CI verifies
schema/behavior.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Contract tests protect service boundaries and are
especially useful when teams deploy independently.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
They do not prove the entire distributed system works together
under production conditions.

T E S T I N G , S E C U R I T Y & O P E R AT I O N A L E XC E L L E N C E
Flaky test
I N O N E B R E AT H
A test that passes or fails nondeterministically without
relevant code changes. Flakiness destroys trust in CI
and hides real regressions.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A smoke alarm that screams randomly teaches
everyone to ignore smoke alarms.
R E A L E X A M P L E
E2E waits fixed 500ms for async UI -> sometimes
fails.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I treat flaky tests as defects: identify nondeterminism,
control time/network/state, and wait for observable
conditions rather than arbitrary sleeps.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Quarantining can be temporary; permanent ignored flakes are
technical debt.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 303 / 310

303 T E S T I N G , S E C U R I T Y & O P E R AT I O N A L E XC E L L E N C E

Flaky test

I N O N E B R E AT H

A test that passes or fails nondeterministically without relevant code changes. Flakiness destroys trust in CI and hides real regressions.

M A K E I T S T I C K

A smoke alarm that screams randomly teaches everyone to ignore smoke alarms.

R E A L E X A M P L E

E2E waits fixed 500ms for async UI -> sometimes fails.

S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W

I treat flaky tests as defects: identify nondeterminism, control time/network/state, and wait for observable conditions rather than arbitrary sleeps.

WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

Quarantining can be temporary; permanent ignored flakes are technical debt.

T E S T I N G , S E C U R I T Y & O P E R AT I O N A L E XC E L L E N C E
Stub vs mock vs fake
I N O N E B R E AT H
Different kinds of test doubles: stubs return canned
answers, mocks assert interactions, fakes provide
lightweight working implementations. Choosing the
right double keeps tests focused without simulating the
entire universe.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Stub = actor reads one line; mock = director checks
whether actor said line; fake = cardboard shop that
actually sells pretend groceries.
R E A L E X A M P L E
stub clock.now(); mock email.send called once;
fake in-memory repository.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use test doubles deliberately: fakes for realistic
behavior, stubs for controlled inputs, mocks when
interaction itself is the contract.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Over-mocking implementation details makes refactoring
painful.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 305 / 310

Content Security Policy (CSP)
I N O N E B R E AT H
Browser policy restricting which scripts, styles,
frames, and other resources a page may load/execute.
It is a strong defense-in-depth control against XSS and
unwanted content execution.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The nightclub has a guest list not only for people but
for every DJ, caterer, and delivery van.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self'
'nonce-...'
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
CSP limits allowed content sources and can significantly
reduce XSS impact, especially with nonces/hashes and
no unsafe-inline.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
CSP complements secure rendering; it is not permission to
inject unsafe HTML.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 306 / 310

T E S T I N G , S E C U R I T Y & O P E R AT I O N A L E XC E L L E N C E
Principle of least privilege
I N O N E B R E AT H
Give users/services only the permissions needed for
their current job. It limits blast radius if credentials or
components are compromised.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Do not give the pizza delivery driver keys to the bank
vault because both are “employees.”
R E A L E X A M P L E
image worker gets object-store read/write for
one bucket, not admin cloud credentials.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Least privilege minimizes permissions across users,
services, tokens, and tools so a compromise has fewer
capabilities.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Review permissions over time; privileges tend to accumulate.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 307 / 310

RBAC
I N O N E B R E AT H
Role-Based Access Control assigns permissions to
roles and roles to users. It simplifies permission
management when access maps cleanly to job
functions.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Teachers get classroom keys; librarians get archive
keys; you assign people roles instead of copying
every key list.
R E A L E X A M P L E
role=admin -> users.write; role=viewer ->
users.read.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
RBAC groups permissions by role and is simple to
reason about for many business applications.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Complex resource/context rules may need finer-grained policy
than roles alone.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 308 / 310

T E S T I N G , S E C U R I T Y & O P E R AT I O N A L E XC E L L E N C E
SLO / error budget
I N O N E B R E AT H
An SLO defines a reliability target; the error budget is
the allowed unreliability within that target. It creates a
quantitative trade-off between shipping speed and
reliability work.
M A K E I T S T I C K
If the train promises 99.9% on-time service, the
small allowed delay budget cannot be spent
carelessly in week one.
R E A L E X A M P L E
SLO 99.9% successful requests over 30 days ->
0.1% error budget.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
SLOs turn reliability into an explicit product target; error
budgets help decide when to prioritize stability over
feature velocity.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Choose user-relevant indicators, not vanity uptime metrics.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 310 / 310

segments.text: SLO / error budget

segments.sectionTitle: I N O N E B R E AT H
segments.text: I N O N E B R E AT H

segments.sectionTitle: I N O N E B R E AT H
segments.text: An SLO defines a reliability target; the error budget is the allowed unreliability within that target. It creates a quantitative trade-off between shipping speed and reliability work.

segments.sectionTitle: M A K E I T S T I C K
segments.text: M A K E I T S T I C K

segments.sectionTitle: M A K E I T S T I C K
segments.text: If the train promises 99.9% on-time service, the small allowed delay budget cannot be spent carelessly in week one.

segments.sectionTitle: R E A L E X A M P L E
segments.text: R E A L E X A M P L E

segments.sectionTitle: R E A L E X A M P L E
segments.text: SLO 99.9% successful requests over 30 days -> 0.1% error budget.

segments.sectionTitle: S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
segments.text: S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W

segments.sectionTitle: S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
segments.text: SLOs turn reliability into an explicit product target; error budgets help decide when to prioritize stability over feature velocity.

segments.sectionTitle: WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
segments.text: WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

segments.sectionTitle: WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
segments.text: Choose user-relevant indicators, not vanity uptime metrics.

DRILL 07
S Y S T E M T H I N K I N G
Safe database migration
Scenario
Add a required field to a table with millions of rows
while old app instances still run.
1. Add nullable/backward-compatible column
2. deploy readers/writers
3. backfill in batches
4. verify
5. enforce constraint
6. remove old path later.
Interview pressure test: Production migrations are deployment
choreography, not just ALTER TABLE syntax.

pages.canonicalText:
Your final interview standard
DO NOT SOUND LIKE A GLOSSARY
Definitions are the starting line. Connect each concept to a
real product behavior, trade-off, and failure mode.
DO NOT ARCHITECT FOR EGO
A clear modular monolith can be more senior than five
premature microservices. Choose complexity only when
requirements pay for it.
MEASURE BEFORE OPTIMIZING
Profile React. EXPLAIN ANALYZE the query. Measure hit
rate. Track TTFT. Load-test capacity. Evidence beats
intuition.
PROTECT INVARIANTS AT THE RIGHT LAYER
UI validation helps users. Backend authorization protects
resources. Database constraints protect data. Each layer
has a job.
THINK IN FAILURE PATHS
What if the request returns late? The cache is stale? The
worker crashes? The model hallucinates? The replica lags?
That is mid-level thinking.
